title: Level 3 (Advanced) - D-2
notes:
West leads the ♥J against 3NT. It seems natural to play the ♥K or ♥Q from dummy, but if South does so the contract will fail on the above layout. East will win the ♥A and return a heart to drive out dummy's remaining honor. As soon as West wins the ♦A he will cash enough heart tricks to defeat the contract.

South can succeed in the above layout by ducking the opening lead in the dummy. If West continues hearts to East's ♥A, East will be out of hearts and the suit will still be stopped when West wins the ♦A. If West switches to clubs instead of continuing hearts at trick 2, South can win in the dummy and knock out the ♦A to establish enough tricks for the contract (4 spades, 3 diamonds, and 2 clubs).

The recommended duck in dummy at trick 1 will work poorly when West was dealt 5 hearts headed by the ♥AJ10 and the ♦A. The ♥J will win the first trick and West will clear hearts. West will later win the ♦A and 2 more heart tricks to defeat the contract.

The above distribution, where ducking the first trick in the dummy leads to defeat, is unlikely as most West players holding 5 hearts to the ♥AJ10 and the ♦A would have overcalled 1♥ after South's 1♦.

The above layout, where ducking at trick 1 is necessary to make the contract, is more likely given West's Pass over 1♦. This makes it correct to duck the opening lead in the dummy. If the East-West hearts are divided 4-3 the recommended play could give up an overtrick, but it will never cost the contract.
